chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it, that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed [the people] on the Day of the Camel.

So he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! I came to these people, invited them, and argued with them, so they invited me to wait for the executioner and to step forward for spear-throwing. So for their mother is the bereavement. I have been, and am not, threatened by war, nor am I scared by the striking. I am the one who blunted their sharp edges and dispersed their groups. With that heart, I face my enemy, and I am upon what my Lord promised me of victory, support, and triumph. And I am upon conviction from my Lord and without doubt in my affair.'

O people! Death does not miss the one who stays, nor does it frustrate the one who flees. There is no escape from death, and whoever does not die is killed. And indeed, the best of deaths is being killed. And by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a thousand strikes with the sword are easier upon me than death upon a bed.

And wonder at Talha, who rallied the people against the son of Affan, until when he was killed, he gave me his clasp with his right hand willingly, then he broke his allegiance to me. O Allah! Seize him and do not delay him.
And indeed Al-Zubayr broke his allegiance to me, cut off my kinship, and backed my enemy against me, so suffice him today with whatever You desire.

key_terms.أَفْضَلَ الْمَوْتِ الْقَتْلُ: The best of deaths is being killed (martyrdom)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.ابْنُ عَفَّانَ: Son of Affan, referring to Uthman ibn Affan
key_terms.فَلَلْتُ حَدَّهُمْ: I blunted their sharp edges (metaphor for weakening their strength)
key_terms.نَكَثَ بَيْعَتِي: He broke his pledge of allegiance
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجَمَلِ: The Day of the Camel, referring to the Battle of Basra

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about death and the betrayal of Talha and Zubayr during the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: This sermon from the Day of the Camel highlights Imam Ali’s (as) strategic patience, having invited the rebels to accept his leadership before resorting to force, thereby establishing the legitimacy of his eventual combat. The text underscores the Shia valorization of martyrdom over natural death, famously declaring that a thousand sword strikes are lighter than a death on one's bed. It concludes with a specific critique of Talha and Al-Zubayr, contrasting their initial pledge of allegiance with their subsequent betrayal and kinship rupture.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it, that,

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> addressed on the Day of (the battle of) the Camel, so he<sup>asws</sup> Praised Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and Extolled Him<sup>azwj</sup>, then said: ‘O you people! I<sup>asws</sup> went over to these people and invited them, an argued against them, so they invited me<sup>asws</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should wait for the executioner and duelling of the spears. So for their mothers is the bereavement (mourning), and I<sup>asws</sup> have never been, and am not, threatened by the war, nor am I<sup>asws</sup> scared by the beating with the strikes of the one who throws it.
So it is for others that they should be (scaring like) lightning and thundering, for I<sup>asws</sup> am Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> who blunted their sharp ends and dispersed their groups, and with that I<sup>asws</sup> face my<sup>asws</sup> enemy. And I<sup>asws</sup> am upon what my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Promised me<sup>asws</sup>, from the victory, and the support and the triumph. And I<sup>asws</sup> am upon conviction from my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> and without any doubt from my<sup>asws</sup> affairs.

O you people! The death does not miss the ones staying at home, nor does it frustrate the warrior. There is nothing unavoidable about the death, and the one who does not die is killed, and that the most superior of the deaths is being killed. By the One<sup>azwj</sup> in Whose Hand is my<sup>asws</sup> soul, a thousand strikes by the sword is easier upon me<sup>asws</sup> than death upon a bed.

And how strange of Talha, being the closest of the people to the son of Affan (Usman), until when he was killed, he came to me clasping with his right hand willingly (pledging allegiance). Then he broke his allegiance to me<sup>asws</sup>. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Seize him and give him no respite!

And Al-Zubayr broke his allegiance with me<sup>asws</sup>, and cut off relationship with me<sup>asws</sup>, and backed my<sup>asws</sup> enemies against me, therefore Enshroud him today with whatever You<sup>azwj</sup> so Desire to!’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub who in a marfu’ has said the following: “On the day of Jamal Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, delivered a speech.

He praised and glorified Allah; then said, ‘O people, I came to these people, called them and presented proof in support of my truthfulness. They then called me for a contest. Their mothers will certainly weep for them; I never was and will not feel threatened by war or intimidated by the pounding of swords. No one is able to defeat experience. They should act thunderously with lightening to frighten people other than me. I am abu al-Hassan. I am the one who turned their sharp edge very blunt and dispersed their large united group. With this kind of heart I am ready to face my enemy. I have firm belief in the promise of my Lord of victory, His support and triumph. I have firm belief in my Lord. I have not even a shred of doubt about the truthfulness of my cause.

O people, death does not miss people living at home and those who run away cannot defeat it. There is no escape from death. If one does not die he is killed and the best death is being killed. I swear by the One in whose hand is my soul, enduring a thousand poundings of the sword is easier for me than dying in bed.

It is very strange of Talhah who was very close to the son of ‘Affan, until the time he was killed soon thereafter he extended his right hand to me to pledge allegiance voluntarily; then he disregarded his pledging allegiance with me. O Allah, clinch him without respite.

Zubayr also disregarded his pledge of allegiance with me as well as the good relationship that was his obligation to maintain with me as relatives. He supported my enemies, therefore, O Lord, suffice me against him as You deem proper.’”
